t: The Japanese 31st Division set out with only three weeks' supply of food and ammunition, and its lack of supplies was the decisive factor in the battle.

Fighting at the Deputy Commissioner's bungalow was so close that the tennis court became a no man's land with grenades thrown between trenches, and the Japanese were not driven from it until a tank was dragged up on 13 May.
Satō abandoned Naga Village on 31 May against Mutaguchi's orders, and the two commanders blamed each other afterwards.
dyk: The garrison's water supply point was on GPT Ridge and was captured by the Japanese on the first day of the siege; a small spring on Garrison Hill could be reached only at night.
ev: Imperial General Headquarters approves the U-Go offensive into India
The Japanese 31st Division crosses the Chindwin and spends six days fighting at Sangshak, which delays it by a week
The siege of Kohima begins and the garrison is driven into a small perimeter on Garrison Hill
Troops of 161st Indian Brigade with tanks break through and relieve the garrison
A tank dragged to the summit destroys the Japanese bunkers at the tennis court, clearing Kohima Ridge
Satō abandons Naga Village and the positions north of the road
Troops from Kohima and Imphal meet at Milestone 109, ending the Siege of Imphal
Satō is removed from command and the Japanese offensive is broken off

f.date: 4 April to 22 June 1944, in three stages: the Japanese attack on Kohima ridge (3 to 16 April), the British and Indian counter-attack (18 April to 13 May) and the pursuit (16 May to 22 June)
f.place: Kohima ridge and the surrounding hills, now the capital of Nagaland in north-east India, on the road between Dimapur and Imphal
f.sides: British and British Indian forces, first the garrison under Colonel Hugh Richards (about 2,500, of whom about 1,000 were non-combatants) and then the British 2nd Division and Indian XXXIII Corps under Lieutenant General Montagu Stopford; the Japanese 31st Division under Lieutenant General Kōtoku Satō, part of Lieutenant General Renya Mutaguchi's Fifteenth Army
f.outcome: The Japanese abandoned Kohima ridge in May and the Naga Village in late May, and on 22 June troops from Kohima and Imphal met at Milestone 109, ending the Siege of Imphal. British and Indian forces lost 4,064 men dead, missing and wounded; the Japanese lost at least 5,764 battle casualties in the Kohima area.
